table.ruleA: Add each tank's scheduled inflow for the cycle; volume not enforced.
table.ruleB: Add each segment's scheduled uptake for the cycle; holding volume not enforced.

table.ruleA: Sequential 1 to 6; if contents > volume (strict), excess goes to tank n+1 before it is handled (cascade), tank set to volume; tank 6 excess to outfall total.
table.ruleB: Sequential 1 to 6; if sap > holding volume (strict), excess goes to segment n+1 before it is handled (cascade), segment set to volume; segment 6 excess to sap-loss tally.

table.ruleA: Read contents after Step 2; STEADY with contents >= upper becomes OVERLOADED; OVERLOADED with contents <= lower becomes STEADY; else unchanged; at most one change per cycle; log (cycle, tank, before, after).
table.ruleB: Read sap after step 2; QUIET with sap >= upper becomes SINK-ACTIVE; SINK-ACTIVE with sap <= lower becomes QUIET; else unchanged; at most once per cycle; log (cycle, segment, before, after).

table.step: Step 4 (Discharge and return / Phloem return and respiration)
table.ruleA: Snapshot: amounts from contents at start of step; STEADY floor(c/4), OVERLOADED floor(c/2); apply simultaneously; each tank loses its amount; STEADY amount to outfall; OVERLOADED amount to tank n-1; tank 1 OVERLOADED amount to outfall; volume not enforced.
table.ruleB: Snapshot: amounts from sap at start of step; QUIET floor(s/4), SINK-ACTIVE floor(s/2); applied together; each loses its amount; QUIET amount to loss tally; SINK-ACTIVE amount to segment n-1; segment 1 SINK-ACTIVE amount to loss tally; volume not enforced.

table.ruleA: If sum of all six > 38 (strict; 38 does not fire), every tank becomes floor(c/2); removed amount (c - floor(c/2)) to outfall; log cycle.
table.ruleB: If total > 38 (strictly greater; 38 does not fire), every segment becomes floor(s/2); all removed sap to loss tally; log cycle.

table.ruleA: (a) end contents 1-6, (b) end states, (c) all state changes, (d) bypass cycles, (e) outfall total, (f) balance check start+inflows = end+outfall.
table.ruleB: (a) end sap 1-6, (b) end states, (c) all state changes in order, (d) leaf-drop cycles or 'none', (e) sap-loss tally, (f) balance check start+uptake = end+loss.

table.step: Fixed data (volumes, marks, starts, limit, schedule)
table.ruleA: Vol 10,8,12,6,9,7; upper 7,6,9,5,7,5; lower 3,2,4,2,3,2; start 3,6,6,2,2,1; limit 38; same 5x6 inflow table.
table.ruleB: Identical values and identical 5x6 uptake table.

result.probeWhy: Starts every position at or near its upper mark (several exactly at it) to test the at-or-above rule, and uses maximum inflows so overflow cascades all the way to the end of the line and tank 1 goes OVERLOADED, which exercises the tank-1-return-to-loss branch. Alternating zero rows force state flips back down and test the at-or-below rule. The printed tables never put tank 1 into the cascade from cycle 1. Separately, a 200,000-case random sweep over starts and inputs from 0 to 9 found 0 differences.
result.differingRule: None. Every rule matches once STEADY is mapped to QUIET, OVERLOADED to SINK-ACTIVE, outfall total to sap-loss tally, storm bypass to leaf-drop, and return line to phloem. The two documents also share the same fixed data and the same input schedule.
result.trust: Both routes agree that the documents are the same. I wrote a separate implementation for each document in C:\Users\USER\AppData\Local\Temp\om\desk-fm\P04\sim.py. On the printed tables they produce identical reports: end quantities 6,10,9,7,4,2; halving fired in cycles 1 and 4; loss 76; balance 114 = 114. On the probe they also match: end quantities 4,4,4,3,4,2; halving in cycles 1, 3, 4 and 5; loss 160; balance 181 = 181. A 200,000-case random sweep over inputs 0 to 9 found 0 differences. One limit on that sweep: every random case fired the halving at least once, so a case where halving never fires was not specifically checked by random cases (the line-by-line table comparison still covers that rule). The probe also did not specifically hit a combined total of exactly 38 at Step 5. The table route covers that rule directly, since both documents say strictly greater than 38.
